speaker: Raddatz
text: it was a pre-planned assault by heavily armed men. Wasn’t this a massive intelligence failure, Vice President Biden?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: What is was, it was a tragedy, Martha. It — Chris Stevens was one of our best. We lost three other brave Americans.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: We mourn the loss of these four Americans who were murdered.

speaker: Ryan
text: When you take a look at what has happened just in the last few weeks, they sent the U.N. ambassador out to say that this was because of a protest and a YouTube video. It took the president two weeks to acknowledge that this was a terrorist attack.

speaker: Ryan
text: This Benghazi issue would be a tragedy in and of itself, but unfortunately it’s indicative of a broader problem. And that is what we are watching on our TV screens is the unraveling of the Obama foreign policy, which is making the (inaudible) more chaotic us less safe.

speaker: Raddatz
text: I just want to you about right in the middle of the crisis. Governor Romney, and you’re talking about this again tonight, talked about the weakness; talked about apologies from the Obama administration. Was that really appropriate right in the middle of the crisis?

speaker: Ryan
text: On that same day, the Obama administration had the exact same position. Let’s recall that they disavowed their own statement that they had put out earlier in the day in Cairo. So we had the same position, but we will — it’s never too early to speak out for our values.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: With all due respect, that’s a bunch of malarkey.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And why is that so?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Because not a single thing he said is accurate. First of all…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Be specific.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I will be very specific. Number one, the — this lecture on embassy security — the congressman here cut embassy security in his budget by $300 million below what we asked for, number one. So much for the embassy security piece.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Can we talk — let me go back to Libya.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Yeah, sure.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What were you first told about the attack? Why — why were people talking about protests? When people in the consulate first saw armed men attacking with guns, there were no protesters. Why did that go on (inaudible)?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Because that was exactly what we were told by the intelligence community. The intelligence community told us that. As they learned more facts about exactly what happened, they changed their assessment. That’s why there’s also an investigation headed by Tom Pickering, a leading diplomat from the Reagan years, who is doing an investigation as to whether or not there are any lapses, what the lapses were, so that they will never happen again.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And they wanted more security there.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Well, we weren’t told they wanted more security there. We did not know they wanted more security again. And by the way, at the time we were told exactly — we said exactly what the intelligence community told us that they knew. That was the assessment. And as the intelligence community changed their view, we made it clear they changed their view.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Ryan, I want to ask you about — the Romney campaign talks a lot about no apologies. He has a book called called “No Apologies.” Should the U.S. have apologized for Americans burning Korans in Afghanistan? Should the U.S. apologize for U.S. Marines urinating on Taliban corpses?

speaker: Ryan
text: Oh, gosh, yes. Urinating on Taliban corpses? What we should not apologize for…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Burning Korans, immediately?

speaker: Ryan
text: What — what we should not be apologizing for are standing up for our values. What we should not be doing is saying to the Egyptian people, while Mubarak is cracking down on them, that he’s a good guy and, in the next week, say he ought to go.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let’s move to Iran. I’d actually like to move to Iran, because there’s really no bigger national security…

speaker: Ryan
text: Absolutely.

speaker: Raddatz
text: … this country is facing. Both President Obama and Governor Romney have said they will prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, even if that means military action. Last week, former Defense Secretary Bob Gates said a strike on Iran’s facilities would not work and, quote, “could prove catastrophic, haunting us for generations.” Can the two of you be absolutely clear and specific to the American people how effective would a military strike be? Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: We cannot allow Iran to gain a nuclear weapons capability. Now, let’s take a look at where we’ve gone — come from. When Barack Obama was elected, they had enough fissile material — nuclear material to make one bomb. Now they have enough for five. They’re racing toward a nuclear weapon. They’re four years closer toward a nuclear weapons capability.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: It’s incredible. Look, imagine had we let the Republican Congress work out the sanctions. You think there’s any possibility the entire world would have joined us, Russia and China, all of our allies? These are the most crippling sanctions in the history of sanctions, period. Period.

speaker: Ryan
text: We want to prevent war.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: And the interesting thing is, how are they going to prevent war? How are they going to prevent war if they say there’s nothing more that we — that they say we should do than what we’ve already done, number one.

speaker: Ryan
text: Martha? Let’s…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan? RYAN: Let’s look at this from the view of the ayatollahs. What do they see? They see this administration trying to water down sanctions in Congress for over two years. They’re moving faster toward a nuclear weapon. They’re spinning the centrifuges faster.

speaker: Raddatz
text: How do you do it so quickly? Look, you — you both saw Benjamin Netanyahu hold up that picture of a bomb with a red line and talking about the red line being in spring. So can you solve this, if the Romney-Ryan ticket is elected, can you solve this in two months before spring and avoid nuclear — nuclear…

speaker: Ryan
text: We can debate a time line. We can debate the time line, whether there’s — it’s that short a time or longer. I agree that it’s probably longer.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You don’t agree with that bomb and whether the Israelis…

speaker: Ryan
text: I don’t want to go into classified stuff. But we both agree that to do this peacefully you’ve got to get them to change their minds. They’re not changing their minds. And look at what this administration…

speaker: Raddatz
text: But what — what do…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Let me tell you what the ayatollah sees.

speaker: Ryan
text: You have to have credibility.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: The ayatollah sees his economy being crippled. The ayatollah sees that there are 50 percent fewer exports of oil. He sees the currency going into the tank. He sees the economy going into freefall. And he sees the world for the first time totally united in opposition to him getting a nuclear weapon.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What does that mean, a bunch of stuff?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Well, it means it’s simply inaccurate.

speaker: Ryan
text: It’s Irish.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: It — it is.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Thanks for the translation. OK.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: We Irish call it malarkey. But last thing. The secretary of defense has made it absolutely clear, we didn’t walk anything back. We will not allow the Iranians to get a nuclear weapon. What Bibi held up there was when they get to the point where they can enrich uranium enough to put into a weapon. They don’t have a weapon to put it into.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I don’t know what world this guy’s living in. RYAN: Thank heavens we had these sanctions in place. It’s in spite of their opposition.

speaker: Ryan
text: They’ve given 20 waivers to this sanction. And all I have to point to are the results. They’re four years closer toward a nuclear weapon. I think that case speaks for itself.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Can you tell the American people…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: By the way, they…

speaker: Raddatz
text: What’s worse, another war in the Middle East…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: … they are not four years closer to a nuclear weapon.

speaker: Ryan
text: Of course they are.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: They’re — they’re closer to being able to get enough fissile material to put in a weapon if they had a weapon.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You are acting a little bit like they don’t want one.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Oh, I didn’t say — no, I’m not saying that. But facts matter, Martha. You’re a foreign policy expert. Facts matter. All this loose talk about them, “All they have to do is get to enrich uranium in a certain amount and they have a weapon,” not true. Not true.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What about Bob Gates’ statement? Let me read that again, “could prove catastrophic, haunting us for generations.”

speaker: Joe Biden
text: He is right. It could prove catastrophic, if we didn’t do it with precision.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: And what it does is it undermines our credibility by backing up the point when we make it that all options are on the table. That’s the point. The ayatollahs see these kinds of statements and they think, “I’m going to get a nuclear weapon.”

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Martha, let me tell you what Russia…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Well, let me ask you what’s worse, war in the Middle East, another war in the Middle East, or a nuclear-armed Iran?

speaker: Ryan
text: I’ll tell you what’s worse. I’ll tell you what’s worse.

speaker: Ryan
text: A nuclear-armed Iran which triggers a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. This is the world’s largest sponsor of — of terrorism. They’ve dedicated themselves…

speaker: Ryan
text: … to wiping an entire country off the map. They call us the Great Satan. And if they get nuclear weapons, other people in the neighborhood will pursue their nuclear weapons, as well.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden?

speaker: Ryan
text: We can’t live with that.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: War should always be the absolute last resort. That’s why these crippling sanctions, which Bibi Netanyahu says we should continue, which — if I’m not mistaken — Governor Romney says we — we should continue. I may be mistaken. He changes his mind so often, I could be wrong.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Gentlemen, I want to bring the conversation to a different kind of national security issue, the state of our economy. The number-one issue here at home is jobs. The percentage of unemployed just fell below 8 percent for the first time in 43 months. The Obama administration had projected that it would fall below 6 percent now after the addition of close to a trillion dollars in stimulus money.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I don’t know how long it will take. We can and we will get it under 6 percent. Let’s look at — let’s take a look at the facts. Let’s look at where we were when we came to office. The economy was in free fall. We had — the great recession hit; 9 million people lost their job; $1.7 — $1.6 trillion in wealth lost in equity in your homes, in retirement accounts for the middle class.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: They’re pushing the continuation of a tax cut that will give an additional $500 billion in tax cuts to 120,000 families. And they’re holding hostage the middle class tax cut because they say we won’t pass — we won’t continue the middle class tax cut unless you give the tax cut for the super wealthy.

speaker: Ryan
text: Joe and I are from similar towns. He’s from Scranton, Pennsylvania. I’m from Janesville, Wisconsin. You know what the unemployment rate in Scranton is today?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I sure do.

speaker: Ryan
text: It’s 10 percent.

speaker: Ryan
text: You know what it was the day you guys came in — 8.5 percent.

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s how it’s going all around America.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: You don’t read the statistics. That’s not how it’s going. It’s going down.

speaker: Raddatz
text: (inaudible) two-minute answer (inaudible)

speaker: Ryan
text: Look, did they come in and inherit a tough situation? Absolutely. But we’re going in the wrong direction. Look at where we are. The economy is barely limping along. It’s growing a 1.3 percent. That’s slower than it grew last year and last year was slower than the year before.

speaker: Ryan
text: He talks about Detroit. Mitt Romney’s a car guy. They keep misquoting him, but let me tell you about the Mitt Romney I know. This is a guy who I was talking to a family in Northborough, Massachusetts the other day, Sheryl and Mark Nixon. Their kids were hit in a car crash, four of them. Two of them, Rob and Reed, were paralyzed. The Romneys didn’t know them. They went to the same church; they never met before.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: But I always say what I mean. And so does Romney.

speaker: Ryan
text: We want everybody to succeed. We want to get people out of poverty, in the middle class, onto a life of self-sufficiently. We believe in opportunity and upward mobility. That’s what we’re going to push for in a Romney administration.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice president? I have a feeling you have a few things to say here.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: The idea — if you heard that — that little soliloquy on 47 percent and you think he just made a mistake, then I think you’re — I — I think — I got a bridge to sell you.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: Let’s not forget that they came in with one-party control. When Barack Obama was elected, his party controlled everything. They had the ability to do everything of their choosing. And look at where we are right now.

speaker: Raddatz
text: When could you get it below 6 percent?

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s what our entire premise of our pro-growth plan for a stronger middle class is all about: getting the economy growing at 4 percent, creating 12 million jobs over the next four years.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Go ahead. Go ahead.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Martha, look. His colleague…

speaker: Ryan
text: Crony capitalism and corporate welfare.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: … runs an investigative committee, spent months and months and months going into this.

speaker: Ryan
text: This is the — this is the inspector general.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Months and months. They found no evidence of cronyism.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You did ask for stimulus money, correct?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Sure he did. By the way…

speaker: Ryan
text: On two occasions we — we — we advocated for constituents who were applying for grants. That’s what we do. We do that for all constituents who are…

speaker: Ryan
text: Was it a good idea to spend taxpayer dollars on electric cars in Finland, or on windmills in China?

speaker: Ryan
text: Was it a good idea to borrow all this money from countries like China and spend it on all these various different interest groups?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Let me tell you what was a good idea. It was a good idea, Moody’s and others said that this was exactly what we needed to stop this from going off the cliff. It set the conditions to be able to grow again. We have, in fact, 4 percent of those green jobs didn’t go under — went under, didn’t work. It’s a better batting average than investment bankers have. They have about a 40 percent…

speaker: Ryan
text: Where are the 5 million green jobs that were being…

speaker: Raddatz
text: I want to move on here to Medicare and entitlements. I think we’ve gone over this quite enough.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: By the way, any letter you send me, I’ll entertain.

speaker: Ryan
text: I appreciate that, Joe.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let’s talk about Medicare and entitlements. Both Medicare and Social Security are going broke and taking a larger share of the budget in the process.

speaker: Ryan
text: Absolutely. Medicare and Social Security are going bankrupt. These are indisputable facts.

speaker: Ryan
text: And then they put this new Obamacare board in charge of cutting Medicare each and every year in ways that will lead to denied care for current seniors.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden, two minutes.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: You know, I heard that death panel argument from Sarah Palin. It seems every vice presidential debate I hear this kind of stuff about panels.

speaker: Ryan
text: Here’s the problem. They got caught with their hands in the cookie jar, turning Medicare into a piggybank for Obamacare. Their own actuary from the administration came to Congress and said one out of six hospitals and nursing homes are going to go out of business as a result of this.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s not what they said.

speaker: Ryan
text: 7.4 million seniors are projected to lose their current Medicare Advantage coverage they have. That’s a $3,200 benefit cut.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That didn’t happen.

speaker: Ryan
text: What we’re saying…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: More people signed up.

speaker: Ryan
text: These are from your own actuaries.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: More — more — more people signed up for Medicare Advantage after the change.

speaker: Ryan
text: What — there’s…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Nobody is…

speaker: Ryan
text: Mr. Vice President, I know…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: No, this is…

speaker: Ryan
text: Mr. Vice President, I know you’re under a lot of duress to make up for lost ground, but I think people would be better served if we don’t keep interrupting each other.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Well, don’t take all the four minutes then.

speaker: Ryan
text: Let me just — let me just say this. We are not — we’re saying don’t change benefits for people 55 and above. They already organized their retirement around these promises.

speaker: Ryan
text: … programs for those of us.

speaker: Raddatz
text: But let — let me ask you this. What — what is your specific plan for seniors who really can’t afford to make up the difference in the value of what you call a premium support plan and others call a voucher?

speaker: Ryan
text: Hundred percent coverage…

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s what we’re saying. So we’re saying…

speaker: Raddatz
text: How do you make that up?

speaker: Ryan
text: … income adjusts (inaudible) these premium support payments by taking down the subsidies for wealthy people.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: There’s not one Democrat who endorses it.

speaker: Ryan
text: It’s a plan…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Not one Democrat who (inaudible).

speaker: Ryan
text: Our partner is a Democrat from Oregon.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: And he said he does no longer support (inaudible).

speaker: Ryan
text: We — we — we put it — we put it together with the former Clinton budget director.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Who disavows it.

speaker: Ryan
text: This idea — this idea came from the Clinton commission to save Medicare chaired by Senator John Breaux.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Which was rejected.

speaker: Ryan
text: If we don’t — if we don’t fix this problem pretty soon then current seniors get cut. Here’s the problem: 10,000 people are retiring every single day in America today and they will for 20 years. That’s not a political thing, that’s a math thing.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Martha, if we just did one thing, if we just — if they just allowed Medicare to bargain for the cost of drugs like Medicaid can, that would save $156 billion right off the bat.

speaker: Ryan
text: And it would deny seniors choices.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: All — all — all…

speaker: Ryan
text: It has a restricted…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Seniors are not denied.

speaker: Ryan
text: Absolutely.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: They are not denied.

speaker: Ryan
text: Because it’s working well right now.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Because we’ve changed the law.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden, let me ask you, if it could help solve the problem, why not very slowly raise the Medicare eligibility age by two years, as Congressman Ryan suggests?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Look, I was there when we did that with Social Security in 1983. I was one of eight people sitting in the room that included Tip O’Neill negotiating with President Reagan. We all got together and everybody said, as long as everybody’s in the deal, everybody’s in the deal, and everybody is making some sacrifice, we can find a way.

speaker: Ryan
text: A voucher is you go to your mailbox, get a check, and buy something. Nobody’s proposing that. Barack Obama four years ago running for president said if you don’t have any fresh ideas, use stale tactics to scare voters. If you don’t have a good record to run on, paint your opponent as someone people should run from.

speaker: Ryan
text: Make a big election about small ideas.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You were one of the few lawmakers to stand with President Bush when he was seeking to partially privatize Social Security.

speaker: Ryan
text: For younger people. What we said then, and what I’ve always agreed is let younger Americans have a voluntary choice of making their money work faster for them within the Social Security system.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: You saw how well that worked.

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s not what Mitt Romney’s proposing. What we’re saying is no changes for anybody 55 and above.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: What Mitt Romney is proposing…

speaker: Ryan
text: And then the kinds of changes we’re talking about for younger people like myself is don’t increase the benefits for wealthy people as fast as everybody else. Slowly raise the retirement age over time.

speaker: Ryan
text: It wouldn’t get to the age of 70 until the year 2103 according to the actuaries.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Quickly, Vice President?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Quickly. The bottom line here is that all the studies show that if we went with Social Security proposal made by Mitt Romney, if you’re 40 — in your 40s now you will pay $2,600 a year — you get $2,600 a year less in Social Security. If you’re in your 20s now, you get $4,700 (inaudible) less.

speaker: Ryan
text: That statistic was completely misleading. But more importantly…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s — there are the facts right…

speaker: Ryan
text: This is what politicians do when they don’t have a record to run on: try to scare people from voting for you. If you don’t get ahead of this problem, it’s going to…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Medicare beneficiaries — there are more beneficiaries…

speaker: Raddatz
text: We’re going to — we’re going to move…

speaker: Raddatz
text: … very simple question…

speaker: Ryan
text: We’re not going to run away. Medicare and Social Security did so much for my own family. We are not going to jeopardize this program, but we have to save it…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: You are jeopardizing this program. You’re changing the program from a guaranteed benefit to premium support. Whatever you call it, the bottom line is people are going to have to pay more money out of their pocket and the families I know and the families I come from, they don’t have the money to pay more out…

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s why we’re saying more for lower income people and less for higher income people.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Gentlemen, I would like to move on to a very simple question for both of you, and something tells me I won’t get a very simple answer, but let me ask you this.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I gave you a simple answer. He’s raising the cost of Medicare.

speaker: Raddatz
text: OK, on to taxes. If your ticket is elected, who will pay more in taxes? Who will pay less? And we’re starting with Vice President Biden for two minutes.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: The middle class will pay less and people making $1 million or more will begin to contribute slightly more. Let me give you one concrete example. The continuation of the Bush tax cuts — we are arguing that the Bush tax cuts for the wealthy should be allowed to expire. Of the Bush tax cuts for the wealthy, $800 million — billion of that goes to people making a minimum of $1 million.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman?

speaker: Ryan
text: Our entire premise of these tax reform plans is to grow the economy and create jobs. It’s a plan that’s estimated to create 7 million jobs. Now, we think that government taking 28 percent of a family and business’s income is enough. President Obama thinks that the government ought to be able to take as much as 44.8 percent of a small business’s income.

speaker: Ryan
text: Look, if you taxed every person and successful business making over $250,000 at 100 percent, it would only run the government for 98 days. If everybody who paid income taxes last year, including successful small businesses, doubled their income taxes this year, we’d still have a $300 billion deficit. You see? There aren’t enough rich people and small businesses to tax to pay for all their spending.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Well, let’s talk about this 20 percent. You have refused — and, again — to offer specifics on how you pay for that 20 percent across-the-board tax cut. Do you actually have the specifics? Or are you still working on it, and that’s why you won’t tell voters?

speaker: Ryan
text: Different than this administration, we actually want to have big bipartisan agreements. You see, I understand the…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Do you have the specifics? Do you have the…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Do you know exactly what you’re doing?

speaker: Ryan
text: Look — look at what Mitt Romney — look at what Ronald Reagan and Tip O’Neill did. They worked together out of a framework to lower tax rates and broaden the base, and they worked together to fix that.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Can I translate?

speaker: Ryan
text: … so we can lower tax rates across the board. Now, here’s why I’m saying this. What we’re saying is, here’s the framework…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I hope I’m going to get time to respond to this.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You’ll get time.

speaker: Ryan
text: We want to work with Congress — we want to work with the Congress on how best to achieve this. That means successful. Look…

speaker: Raddatz
text: No specifics, again.

speaker: Ryan
text: Mitt — what we’re saying is, lower tax rates 20 percent, start with the wealthy, work with Congress to do it…

speaker: Raddatz
text: And you guarantee this math will add up?

speaker: Ryan
text: Absolutely. Six studies have guaranteed — six studies have verified that this math adds up. But here’s…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: .. let me translate. Let me have a chance to translate.

speaker: Ryan
text: I’ll come back in a second, then, right?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: First of all, I was there when Ronald Reagan tax breaks — he gave specifics of what he was going to cut, number one, in terms of tax expenditures. Number two, 97 percent of the small businesses in America pay less — make less than $250,000. Let me tell you who some of those other small businesses are: hedge funds that make $600 million, $800 million a year. That’s — that’s what they count as small businesses, because they’re pass- through.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Now, there’s not enough — the reason why the AEI study, the American Enterprise Institute study, the Tax Policy Center study, the reason they all say it’s going — taxes go up on the middle class, the only way you can find $5 trillion in loopholes is cut the mortgage deduction for middle-class people, cut the health care deduction, middle-class people, take away their ability to get a tax break to send their kids to college. That’s why they arrive at it.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Is he wrong about that?

speaker: Ryan
text: He is wrong about that. They’re…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: How’s that?

speaker: Ryan
text: You can — you can cut tax rates by 20 percent and still preserve these important preferences for middle-class taxpayers…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Not mathematically possible.

speaker: Ryan
text: It is mathematically possible. It’s been done before. It’s precisely what we’re proposing.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: It has never been done before.

speaker: Ryan
text: It’s been done a couple of times, actually.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: It has never been done before.

speaker: Ryan
text: Jack Kennedy lowered tax rates, increased growth. Ronald Reagan…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Oh, now you’re Jack Kennedy?

speaker: Ryan
text: Ronald Reagan — Republicans and Democrats…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: This is amazing.

speaker: Ryan
text: Republican and Democrats have worked together on this.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s right.

speaker: Ryan
text: You know, I understand you guys aren’t used to doing bipartisan deals…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: But we told each other what we’re going to do.

speaker: Ryan
text: Republicans and Democrats…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: When we did it Reagan, we said, here — here are the things we’re going to cut.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s what we said.

speaker: Ryan
text: We said here’s the framework, let’s work together to fill in the details. That’s exactly…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Fill in the detail.

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s how you get things done. You work with Congress — look, let me say it this way.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s coming from a Republican Congress working bipartisanly, 7 percent rating? Come on.

speaker: Ryan
text: Mitt Romney was governor of Massachusetts, where 87 percent of the legislators he served, which were Democrats. He didn’t demonize them. He didn’t demagogue them. He met with those party leaders every week. He reached across the aisle. He didn’t compromise principles.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: And you saw what happened.

speaker: Ryan
text: He found common ground — and he balanced the budget…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: You saw — if he did such a great job…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Vice President…

speaker: Ryan
text: … four times without raising taxes…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Why isn’t he even contesting Massachusetts?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Vice President, what would you suggest — what would you suggest beyond raising taxes on the wealthy, that would substantially reduce the long-term deficit?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Just let the taxes expire like they’re supposed to on those millionaires. We don’t — we can’t afford $800 billion going to people making a minimum of $1 million. They do not need it, Martha. Those 120,000 families make $8 million a year. Middle-class people need the help. Why does my friend cut out the tuition tax credit for them? Why does he go after the childcare…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Can you declare anything off-limits?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Why do they do that?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Can you declare anything off-limits?

speaker: Ryan
text: Yeah, we’re saying close loopholes…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Home mortgage deduction?

speaker: Ryan
text: … on high-interest people.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Home mortgage deduction?

speaker: Ryan
text: For higher-income people. Here…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Can you guarantee that no one making less than $100,000 will have a mortgage — their mortgage deduction impacted? Guarantee?

speaker: Ryan
text: This taxes a million small businesses. He keeps trying to make you think that it’s just some movie star or hedge fund guy or an actor…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Ninety-seven percent of the small businesses make less than $250,000 a year, would not be affected.

speaker: Ryan
text: Joe, you know it hits a million — this taxes a million people, a million small businesses.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Does it tax 97 percent of the American businesses?

speaker: Ryan
text: It taxes a million small businesses…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Small businesses?

speaker: Ryan
text: … who are our greatest job creators.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I wish I’d get — the “greatest job creators” are the hedge fund guys.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And you’re — and you’re going to increase the defense budget.

speaker: Ryan
text: Think about it this way.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And you’re going to increase the defense budget.

speaker: Ryan
text: No, we’re not just going to cut the defense budget like they’re — they’re proposing…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: They’re going to increase it $2 billion.

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s not…

speaker: Ryan
text: We’re talking about… RADDATZ: So no massive defense increases?

speaker: Ryan
text: No, we’re saying don’t — OK, you want to get into defense now?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Yes, I do. I do, because that’s another math question.

speaker: Ryan
text: So — right, OK.

speaker: Raddatz
text: How do you do that?

speaker: Ryan
text: So they proposed a $478 billion cut to defense to begin with. Now we have another $500 billion cut to defense that’s lurking on the horizon. They insisted upon that cut being involved in the debt negotiations, and so we have a $1 trillion cut…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let’s put the automatic defense cuts aside, OK?

speaker: Ryan
text: Right, OK.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let’s put those aside. No one wants that.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I’d like to go back to that.

speaker: Raddatz
text: But I want to know how you do the math and have this increase in defense spending?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Two trillion dollars.

speaker: Ryan
text: You don’t cut defense by a trillion dollars. That’s what we’re talking about.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And what — what national security issues justify an increase?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Who’s cutting it by $1 trillion?

speaker: Ryan
text: We’re going to cut 80,000 soldiers, 20,000 Marines, 120 cargo planes. We’re going to push the Joint Strike Fighter out…

speaker: Raddatz
text: Drawing down in one war and one war…

speaker: Ryan
text: If these cuts go through, our Navy will be the smallest — the smallest it has been since before World War I.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Quickly, Vice President Biden on this. I want to move on.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Look, we don’t cut it. And I might add, this so-called — I know we don’t want to use the fancy word “sequester,” this automatic cut — that was part of a debt deal that they asked for.

speaker: Ryan
text: Can I tell you what that meant?

speaker: Ryan
text: We’ve been looking for bipartisanship for a long time.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: And so the bipartisanship is what he voted for, the automatic cuts in defense if they didn’t act.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Some of the military.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Not some of the military. That was the decision of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, recommended to us and agreed to by the president. That is a fact.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Who answers to a civilian leader.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: They made the recommendation first.

speaker: Raddatz
text: OK. Let’s move on to Afghanistan.

speaker: Ryan
text: Can I get into that for a second?

speaker: Raddatz
text: I’d like to move on to Afghanistan please. And that’s one of the biggest expenditures this country has made, in dollars, and more importantly in lives.

speaker: Ryan
text: We don’t want to lose the gains we’ve gotten. We want to make sure that the Taliban does not come back in and give Al Qaida a safe haven.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Martha, let’s keep our eye on the ball. The reason — I’ve been in and out of Afghanistan and Iraq 20 times. I’ve been up in the Konar (ph) Valley. I’ve been throughout that whole country, mostly in a helicopter, and sometimes in a vehicle.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What — what conditions could justify staying, Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: We don’t want to stay. We want — look, one of my best friends in Janesville, a reservist, is at a forward-operating base in eastern Afghanistan right now. Our wives are best friends. Our daughters are best friends. I want — I want him and all of our troops to come home as soon and safely as possible.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let me go back to this. He says we’re absolutely leaving in 2014. You’re saying that’s not an absolute, but you won’t talk about what conditions would justify…

speaker: Ryan
text: Do you know why we say that?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I’d like to know…

speaker: Ryan
text: Because we don’t want to broadcast to our enemies “put a date on your calendar, wait us out, and then come back.” We want to make sure…

speaker: Raddatz
text: But you agree with the timeline.

speaker: Ryan
text: We do agree — we do agree with the timeline and the transition, but what we — what any administration will do in 2013 is assess the situation to see how best to complete this timeline. What we do not want to do…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: We will leave in 2014.

speaker: Ryan
text: … what we don’t want to do is give our allies reason to trust us less and our enemies more — we don’t want to embolden our enemies to hold and wait out for us and then take over…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Martha, that’s a bizarre statement.

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s why we want to make sure — no, that’s why we want to make sure that…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Forty-nine of our allies — hear me — 49 of our allies signed on to this position.

speaker: Ryan
text: And we’re reading that they want to…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Forty-nine — 49 of our allies said “out in 2014.” It’s the responsibility of the Afghans. We have other responsibilities… (CROSSTALK)

speaker: Raddatz
text: Do you really think that this timeline…

speaker: Ryan
text: Which is — which is…

speaker: Raddatz
text: We have — we have soldiers and Marines. We have Afghan forces murdering our forces over there. The Taliban is, do you think, taking advantage of this timeline?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Look, the Taliban — what we’ve found out, and we — you saw it in Iraq, Martha, unless you set a timeline, Baghdad, in the case of Iraq, and — and Kabul, in the case of Afghanistan will not step up. They’re happy to let us continue to do the job; international security forces to do the job.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let me go back.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s the only way it works.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let me go back to the — the surge troops that we put in there. And — and you brought this up, Congressman Ryan. I have talked to a lot of troops. I’ve talked to senior offices who were concerned that the surge troops were pulled out during the fighting season, and some of them saw that as a political — as a political move. So can you tell me, Vice President Biden, what was the military reason for bringing those surge troops home…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: The military reason…

speaker: Raddatz
text: … before the fighting had ended?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: … was bringing — by the way, when the president announced the surge, you’ll remember, Martha, he said the surge will be out by the end of the summer. The military said the surge will be out. Nothing political about this.

speaker: Raddatz
text: The military follows orders. I mean, there — trust me. There are people who were concerned about pulling out on the fighting season.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Sure. There are people that are concerned, but not the Joint Chiefs. That was their recommendation in the Oval Office to the president of the United States of America. I sat there. I’m sure you’ll find someone who disagrees with the Pentagon. I’m positive you’ll find that within the military. But that’s not the case here.

speaker: Ryan
text: Let me try and illustrate the issue here, because I think this — it can get a little confusing. We’ve all met with General Allen and General Scaparrotti in Afghanistan to talk about fighting seasons.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Fighting season…

speaker: Ryan
text: We’re sending fewer people out in all of these hotspots to do the same job that they were supposed to do a month ago.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Because we turned it over…

speaker: Ryan
text: But we took 22,000 people out…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: … we turned it over to the Afghan troops we trained. No one got pulled out that didn’t get filled in by trained Afghan personnel. And he’s — he’s conflating two issues. The fighting season that Petraeus was talking about and former — and Admiral Mullen was the fighting season this spring. That’s what he was talking about. We did not — we did not pull them out.

speaker: Ryan
text: The calendar works the same every year.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: It does work the same every year. But we’re not staying there…

speaker: Ryan
text: Spring, summer, fall. It’s warm, or it’s not. They’re still fighting us. They’re still coming over the passes. They’re still coming into Zabul, to Kunar, to all of these areas, but we are sending fewer people to the front to fight them. And that’s…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s right, because that’s the Afghan responsibility. We’ve trained them.

speaker: Ryan
text: Not in the east.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let’s move — let’s move to another war.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Not in the east?

speaker: Ryan
text: R.C. East — R.C. East…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: R.C. East is the most dangerous place in the world.

speaker: Ryan
text: That’s right. That’s why we don’t want to send fewer people to the…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s — that’s why we should send Americans in to do the job, instead of the — you’d rather Americans be going in doing the job instead of the trainees?

speaker: Ryan
text: No. We are already sending Americans to do the job, but fewer of them. That’s the whole problem.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s right. We’re sending in more Afghans to do the job, Afghans to do the job.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let’s move to another war, the civil war in Syria, where there are estimates that more — estimates that more than 25,000, 30,000 people have now been killed. In March of last year, President Obama explained the military action taken in Libya by saying it was in the national interest to go in and prevent further massacres from occurring there. So why doesn’t the same logic apply in Syria? Vice President Biden?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Different country. It’s a different country. It is five times as large geographically, it has one-fifth the population, that is Libya, one-fifth the population, five times as large geographically.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: Nobody is proposing to send troops to Syria. American troops.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: What would my friend do differently? If you notice, he never answers the question.

speaker: Ryan
text: No, I would — I — we would not be going through the U.N. in all of these things.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Let me — you don’t go through the U.N. We are in the process now — and have been for months — in making sure that help, humanitarian aid, as well as other aid and training is getting to those forces that we believe, the Turks believe, the Jordanians believe, the Saudis believe are the free forces inside of Syria. That is underway.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What happens if Assad does not fall, Congressman Ryan? What happens to the region? What happens if he hangs on? What happens if he does?

speaker: Ryan
text: Then Iran keeps their greatest ally in the region. He’s a sponsor of terrorism. He’ll probably continue slaughtering his people. We and the world community will lose our credibility on this. Look, he mentioned the reset…

speaker: Raddatz
text: So what would Romney-Ryan do about that credibility?

speaker: Ryan
text: Well, we agree with the same red line, actually, they do on chemical weapons, but not putting American troops in, other than to secure those chemical weapons. They’re right about that.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What’s your criteria…

speaker: Ryan
text: … we should not have — we should not have waited to Russia…

speaker: Raddatz
text: What’s your criteria…

speaker: Ryan
text: … should not have waited for Russia to give us the green light at the U.N. to do something about it.

speaker: Ryan
text: They’re — they’re still arming the man. Iran is flying flights over Iraq…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: And the opposition is being armed.

speaker: Ryan
text: … to help Bashar Assad. And, by the way, if we had the status-of-forces agreement that the vice president said he would bet his vice presidency on in Iraq, we probably would have been able to prevent that. But he failed to achieve that, as well, again.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let me ask you a quick question.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What’s your criteria for intervention?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Yeah. RYAN: In Syria?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Worldwide.

speaker: Ryan
text: What is in the national interests of the American people.

speaker: Raddatz
text: How about humanitarian interests?

speaker: Ryan
text: What is in the national security of the American people. It’s got to be in the strategic national interests of our country.

speaker: Raddatz
text: No humanitarian?

speaker: Ryan
text: Each situation will — will come up with its own set of circumstances, but putting American troops on the ground? That’s got to be within the national security interests of the American people.

speaker: Raddatz
text: I want to — we’re — we’re almost out of time here.

speaker: Ryan
text: That means like embargoes and sanctions and overflights, those are things that don’t put American troops on the ground. But if you’re talking about putting American troops on the ground, only in our national security interests.

speaker: Raddatz
text: I want to move on, and I want to return home for these last few questions. This debate is, indeed, historic. We have two Catholic candidates, first time, on a stage such as this. And I would like to ask you both to tell me what role your religion has played in your own personal views on abortion.

speaker: Raddatz
text: … please talk personally about this, if you could.

speaker: Ryan
text: I don’t see how a person can separate their public life from their private life or from their faith. Our faith informs us in everything we do. My faith informs me about how to take care of the vulnerable, of how to make sure that people have a chance in life.

speaker: Ryan
text: Now, you want to ask basically why I’m pro-life? It’s not simply because of my Catholic faith. That’s a factor, of course. But it’s also because of reason and science.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President Biden?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: My religion defines who I am, and I’ve been a practicing Catholic my whole life. And has particularly informed my social doctrine. The Catholic social doctrine talks about taking care of those who — who can’t take care of themselves, people who need help. With regard to — with regard to abortion, I accept my church’s position on abortion as a — what we call a (inaudible) doctrine. Life begins at conception in the church’s judgment. I accept it in my personal life.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan.

speaker: Ryan
text: All I’m saying is, if you believe that life begins at conception, that, therefore, doesn’t change the definition of life. That’s a principle. The policy of a Romney administration is to oppose abortion with exceptions for rape, incest and life of the mother.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: You have on the issue…

speaker: Ryan
text: … why would they keep — why would they keep suing you? It’s a distinction without a difference.

speaker: Raddatz
text: I want to go back to the abortion question here. If the Romney-Ryan ticket is elected, should those who believe that abortion should remain legal be worried?

speaker: Ryan
text: We don’t think that unelected judges should make this decision; that people through their elected representatives in reaching a consensus in society through the democratic process should make this determination.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: The court — the next president will get one or two Supreme Court nominees. That’s how close Roe v. Wade is. Just ask yourself, with Robert Bork being the chief adviser on the court for — for Mr. Romney, who do you think he’s likely to appoint? Do you think he’s likely to appoint someone like Scalia or someone else on the court far right that would outlaw (inaudible) — outlaw abortion? I suspect that would happen.

speaker: Ryan
text: Was there a litmus test on them?

speaker: Joe Biden
text: There was no litmus test. We picked people who had an open mind; did not come with an agenda.

speaker: Raddatz
text: I’m — I’m going to move on to this closing question because we are running out of time.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I would say to him the same thing I say to my son who did serve a year in Iraq, that we only have one truly sacred obligation as a government. That’s to equip those we send into harm’s way and care for those who come home. That’s the only sacred obligation we have. Everything else falls behind that.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Congressman Ryan?

speaker: Ryan
text: First of all, I’d thank him to his service to our country.

speaker: Ryan
text: We can do better than this.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: I hope I’ll get equal time.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You will get just a few minutes here. A few seconds, really.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: The two budgets the congressman introduced have eviscerated all the things that the middle class cares about. It is (inaudible) he will knock 19 million people off of Medicare. It will kick 200,000 children off of early education. It will eliminate the tax credit people have to be able to send their children to college. It cuts education by $450 billion.

speaker: Raddatz
text: We’re going to — we’re going to the closing statements in a minute.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You’re going to have your closing statement.

speaker: Ryan
text: Not raising taxes is not cutting taxes. And by the way, our budget…

speaker: Joe Biden
text: We have not raised…

speaker: Ryan
text: … by 3 percent a year instead of 4.5 percent like they propose. Not spending more money as much as they say is not a spending cut.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Let me — let me calm down things here just for a minute. And I want to talk to you very briefly before we go to closing statements about your own personal character. If you are elected, what could you both give to this country as a man, as a human being, that no one else could?

speaker: Ryan
text: Honesty, no one else could? There are plenty of fine people who could lead this country. But what you need are people who, when they say they’re going to do something, they go do it. What you need are, when people see problems, they offer solutions to fix those problems. We’re not getting that.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Vice President, can we get to that — to that issue of what you could bring as a man, a human being? And I really — I’m going to keep you to about 15 seconds here.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Well, he gets 40, I get 15, that’s OK.

speaker: Raddatz
text: He didn’t have 40. He didn’t have 40.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: That’s all right.

speaker: Raddatz
text: OK, we now turn to the candidates for their closing statements. Thank you, gentlemen. And that coin toss, again, has Vice President Biden starting with the closing statement.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Well, let — let me say at the outset that I want to thank you, Martha, for doing this, and Centre College. The fact is that we’re in a situation where we inherited a god-awful circumstance. People are in real trouble. We acted to move to bring relief to the people who need the most help now.

speaker: Ryan
text: I want to thank you, as well, Martha, Danville, Kentucky, Centre College, and I want to thank you, Joe. It’s been an honor to engage in this critical debate.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And thank you both again. Thank you very much.

speaker: Joe Biden
text: Thank you.

speaker: Raddatz
text: This concludes the vice presidential debate. Please tune in next Tuesday for the second presidential debate at Hofstra University in New York. I’m Martha Raddatz of ABC News. I do hope all of you go to the polls. Have a good evening.
